title: Kernel catalogue sparsity-aware selector and online autotuner
creator: Aisha Khan
description: Problem: As more open and custom models exhibit structured sparsity (pruned heads, block-sparse FFNs, sparse attention masks from retrieval), our current kernel picker, which mostly indexes dense throughput and seqlen heuristics, begins to make suboptimal choices. Resulting issues are higher P50/P95 latencies on some workloads and increased cost due to running dense kernels where sparse-specialized kernels would be cheaper.
goals: Introduce a sparsity-aware profile into the kernel catalogue metadata (sparsity patterns, mask density, block sizes)

Implement a lightweight online autotuner that observes per-model and per-request sparsity signals (attention mask density, activation sparsity) and biases kernel selection towards sparse-capable kernels when beneficial
Ensure safeguards: fast rollback, safety budget for P95 latency, and stable choices for hot models to avoid oscillation
Expose an operator-configurable knob to prefer cost vs latency for enterprise Dedicated customers
acceptance_criteria: Catalogue metadata updated for top 20 served models with sparsity annotations
Autotuner reduces token cost by >=8% on at least two sampled sparse-heavy workloads without increasing P95 latency by more than 5%
No regression on dense baseline workloads (P50, P95 within 1% of prior) after rollout
Feature gated behind runtime flag and feature toggle per-customer; rollout plan tested in canary cluster
design_decisions: Store sparsity descriptors at model-version level as: global density, per-layer block-sparsity hints, attention-mask-compatibility tags

Autotuner will operate in two phases: exploration (short, randomized trial runs with traffic mirroring) and exploitation (stable preference with decay), using an upper confidence bound style scoring to trade off cost vs latency

We will not attempt to modify kernels at runtime; the system picks among existing kernel implementations (dense, block-sparse, attention-specialized) and a fallback dense kernel when incompatibility is detected
To limit telemetry overhead, capture per-request sparsity metrics only for sampled traffic (1-5% initially) and aggregate into seqlen+sparsity buckets
implementation_steps: Add sparsity metadata schema to kernel catalogue and ingestion pipeline
Instrument runtime to emit lightweight sparsity metrics: attention mask density, FFN activation density, block occupancy
Implement autotuner service: bucketization, scoring, and versioned policy store; integrate with existing kernel picker API
Create rollback and cooldown mechanisms: latency SLO monitors with automated revert on exceedance
Add console UI panel for sparsity-autotune insights and per-customer toggle
Write integration tests and perf harnesses that simulate block-sparse and dense workloads
testing_plan: Unit tests for catalogue metadata CRUD and validation
Synthetic perf benchmarks: run matrix of seqlen(8,32,128,512) x sparsity(very sparse, med, dense) x batch sizes to ensure selector picks expected kernel
Shadow canary: run autotuner in mirror mode on 5% of traffic in canary region for 48 hours and compare picked kernel vs baseline
A/B rollout: 10% traffic with autotune on, monitor cost and P95 for 7 days before promoting
Chaos test: simulate transient GPU slowdowns and verify fallback to latency-preferred kernels maintains SLO
metrics: autotuner exploration ratio and convergence time
rollout_plan: Feature gated, enable catalogue changes in staging and run validation harness
Enable autotuner in mirror-only mode in canary cluster (2 weeks), analyze results
Enable autotuner for 10% of traffic in canary with gradual ramp (48h -> 10% -> 50% -> 100% by application) with automated rollback on SLO deviations
Expose dedicated-customer toggle and run controlled pilots with two Dedicated customers
After stable metrics for 4 weeks, promote to release runtime-1.22 and announce
risks_and_mitigations: Risk: Oscillation between kernels causing performance instability. Mitigation: add cooldown windows and hysteresis in policy selection
Risk: Sparse measurement noise leading to bad choices for low-volume models. Mitigation: require minimum sample counts and fallback to historical default for low-volume models
Risk: Increased telemetry cost. Mitigation: strict sampling and aggregation; only persist aggregated buckets
Risk: Incompatibility with private/on-prem catalog sync. Mitigation: add opt-out flag and provide a lightweight on-prem catalogue sync tool
notes: Spike done by @Miguel (2026-02-20): measured attention-mask density distribution for top 50 models; ~27% show >30% zeroed tokens in typical requests
Decision: prefer catalogue metadata approach over dynamic kernel patching to reduce runtime risk (decision doc linked)
We should coordinate with model-onboarding team to capture sparsity hints at ingestion time
Keep exploration budget default conservative (max 5% traffic per model) and configurable via console
